text.p: The president of the troubled nuclear facility Maine Yankee resigned on Friday, the chairman of the board told reporters at a press conference.
Charles Frizzle resigned following a board of directors' meeting, said David Flanagan, board chairman.
Flanagan said the board wanted to look for new leadership that could deal with "cultural issues" raised in a recent regulatory review.
"It is not the record of the past, but the requirements of the future that led the directors to conclude a change was necessary," Flanagan said in a statement.

A report issued earlier this year following a special inspection of Maine Yankee by state and federal regulators citicized the plant's mangement for allegedly fostering a culture that placed the facility's profitablity over safety concerns. Flanagan said Frizzle would remain in place
temporarily as the search for a successor began.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
